QUESTION.topic: MySQL SET vs bitmask for permissions
QUESTION.r: Agreement on the bitmask approach — but recommend INTEGER over MySQL SET for three reasons: 1. SET is MySQL-specific. INTEGER bitmask is portable to SQLite (which Conduit Fund uses via IndexedDB), PostgreSQL, and any future store. 2. SET enforces an enum at the column level — adding permission 65 requires ALTER TABLE. INTEGER bitmask adds new bits with no schema change. Entropic by design. 3. Bitwise queries (permissions AND 4 = 4) work identically across all engines. Proposed: permissions INTEGER DEFAULT 0. Each permission = power of 2. Check with (record.permissions AND :flag) = :flag.

Read and understood. Comments below — no changes made pending approval.
RELATIONSHIPS (1A-1C): The three-way split (Hierarchical / Network / Temporal) maps cleanly to the ConduitFlow ontology. Temporal relationships are the least modeled in current Conduit Fund schema — sequential and concurrent deal states are tracked via status fields but not as first-class relationship types. Worth formalizing.
BEHAVIORS (2A-2C): CRUD + State + Event-Driven is the right triad. Event-driven actions (triggers, workflows) are currently implicit in the UI — they fire but are not recorded. Recommend adding an event_log table to make them auditable. GeoJS curvature escalation events are a natural source.
CONNECTIONS (2D-2F): Connection distance (degrees of separation) is the most interesting addition here. It maps directly to GeoJS path length in semantic space — a two-hop connection has higher curvature than a direct one. The directional/bidirectional distinction is already in ConduitFlow relationship edges. Connection attributes (type, strength, duration) are currently in Agreements — this formalizes them as first-class edge properties.
STATES (3A-3C): State duration and timing (3C) is not currently tracked in Conduit Fund — only the current state is stored, not how long it has been in that state or what triggered the transition. This is a gap worth closing.
ATTRIBUTES (4A-4C): Derived attributes (4C) are the Emerge.html use case — fields that emerge from computation rather than direct input. The entropic schema handles these naturally since they are just additional observed fields.
SCREENSHOT: Conduit Fund Import/Export panel noted. 4 records in OPCOS, 0 elsewhere. CSV export per table and ZIP all confirmed working. The import side (CSV → field mapping) is the surface most affected by the entropic schema — column mapping will need to handle unknown fields gracefully rather than rejecting them.
